text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today to $127.30, continuing a weak two-week slide that's now down 7.3%. The immediate pressure comes from geopolitical de-escalation: yesterday the U.S. and Iran held talks at the U.N., and while Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal today, the mere fact of diplomacy had already driven U.S. crude oil down nearly 8% for the week. Crude at $96.41 per barrel (down from higher levels earlier in the week) means less revenue per barrel pumped, which directly weighs on oil company stock prices.

The broader context is that oil markets have been whipsawed by supply-shock concerns and Middle East tensions, but signs of diplomatic progress—even tentative ones—pull prices down as investors reduce their "insurance premium" for conflict. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's crude exports keep hitting post-Iran-war highs despite ongoing attacks on its infrastructure, suggesting supply fears may be overblown, which also takes pressure off prices and energy stocks.
